04.note: Two swings, one scrub. ComparePanel already compared the NUMBERS (score, tempo, phase durations); its own prop comment said the reference was 'held by the player so the picture can show it too' and the picture never showed it. It does now: a second FrameClockView beside the first, driven from the leader's frame. THE REAL WORK IS align.ts, and the insight is that frames and seconds are BOTH wrong answers - frame 143 of one swing means nothing in another, and seconds cancel exactly the tempo difference a golfer is comparing. The only shared vocabulary is the swing itself, so the mapping runs position-to-position through the P-codes both artifacts carry: find the segment the leader's frame falls in, take the fraction across it, land at that fraction of the follower's own segment. Differing lengths and differing frame rates both fall out for free. VALIDATED ON REAL DATA, not just the unit tests: all 90 ordered fixture pairs align with zero unalignable and zero non-monotonic or out-of-range frames, and swing1's ten positions map EXACTLY onto pro_3's ten - two swings that differ in length by more than five times (93 frames of swing against 1267). A CAUGHT DESIGN FLAW: anchorsOf originally sorted by FRAME and then checked the frames were strictly increasing, which is vacuous - sorting orders any table into compliance, so a swing whose top was detected before its address would have passed and run the follower backwards through its own swing. It now sorts by P-CODE ORDINAL, which makes the check mean something. Also correct: P10 must sort after P2, which a string compare gets wrong. Refusals are first-class - an unanalysed reference or fewer than two shared positions renders an explicit notice, because a silently misaligned pair looks exactly like a working one. Neither pane wears the other's overlay (two swings' normalized coordinates are not comparable). Oracles green: tsc clean, 283 jest across 26 suites (+17), Metro bundles 6.20MB - JS only, a Reload not a rebuild. NOT DONE, named rather than rounded away: the DEVICE COST. Two ExoPlayer decoders on screen at once, and whether the leader's frame-lock survives it, is the step's own open question and only the phone answers it. Claude did not drive the phone (Taylor's 2026-08-13 standing rule). Nothing about the side-by-side layout has been seen on glass either. Structurally the two players are safe - every piece of frame-clock's state is a per-instance field, no singletons, no companion-object state - but safe is not free. | VERIFIED ON GLASS 2026-08-13 on the desktop emulator: picking 'Pro Swing' put both swings side by side, leader with its overlay and reference clean by design, and scrubbing held them at the SAME POSITION - both at address together at frame 283, both at the top of the backswing together at frame 343 - across a 3.4:1 vs 1.6:1 tempo difference and a five-fold length difference. D52's mapping is visibly correct on real swings. A second ExoPlayer instance initialises cleanly.
